answer: To join the grader set, an agent buys one address-bound identity lease from a rate-limited pool whose remaining depth is published like a lagoon waterline: only as many newcomers as that pool can cover may enter this window. The lease is paid in spendable coin locked until the epoch closes. If a clustering proof later shows two leases share one controller, both are marked hollow and the locked coin is burned, and a crystal revocation bars that funding graph from buying another lease for three epochs, so clone swarms cannot multiply voting weight more cheaply than honest singleton entry.
